packageRules.description: Actions used only by this repo's own CI/CD workflows don't affect consumers, so keep them as chores - no need to cut a release for internal tooling bumps.

Runtime dependencies ship with the tool, so a bump is user-facing. config:recommended already commits them as 'fix' (a patch release, listed under Bug Fixes); commit them as 'build' instead so release-please lists them under Dependencies and still cuts a patch release (see release-please-config.json). Dev tooling keeps the default 'chore' and does not release.

The Bun pin ships twice, since the release binaries and the container image both embed that Bun, so its bump is user-facing: commit it as 'build', as the runtime dependencies are, so release-please lists it under Dependencies and cuts a patch release. Renovate moves it in one pull request, because the Dockerfile's oven/bun tag must equal the pin of mise.toml (src/dockerfile.spec.ts): bun is the dependency name of the mise manager's pin and of the packageManager field of package.json, and docker.io/oven/bun is the Dockerfile's image. Node, dev tooling and CI actions keep the default 'chore' and do not release.
Every other image of the Dockerfile ships in the container image too (the distroless runtime), so a bump of it is user-facing: commit it as 'build', as the runtime dependencies are.

TypeScript 7 is the native compiler and ships no JavaScript API, which typescript-eslint, and so the lint job, needs; TypeScript 7.1 is expected to bring a new one. Stay below 7 until typescript-eslint supports it: 6.x passes the typecheck, the lint and the suite, and builds the same dist/ as 5.9.
this-is-tobi/github-workflows is referenced via its moving v0 major tag on purpose - don't pin or bump it.
